title: Chapter 34: The Witch, the Spirit, and the Magician
content:
Chapter 34:

The Witch, the Spirit, and the Magician

—The Witch of Envy, Satella.

A paranormal entity feared by everything in the world, who wiped out the witches that once made the world scream, and destroyed half the world with the power she stole.

It’s said her body was sealed inside a crystal by the hands of a hero, and even now, unable to be destroyed, she remains sealed away.

A totally absurd story, Subaru thought with the sensibilities of a modern kid.

Going by the common sense of his original world, it was an impossible tale. It was one thing for her evil deeds to be passed down for hundreds of years, but the idea that such an entity was still slumbering somewhere in the world right now?

“Well, it’s an era where people might not know the president’s name but they know the most popular girl in the national idol group, so I guess common sense isn’t that reliable.”

Then again, Subaru himself was the prime example of someone who lived a typically bland, apathetic life, having no interest in either of those things.

With those thoughts in mind, Subaru chewed over what Beatrice had told him, resting his chin in his hand as he looked over.

In the garden bathed in the morning sun, Emilia sat on the greenery, pale lights floating around her.

No matter how many times it was repeated, its fantastical impression never faded—one of the most beautiful sights in this world: Emilia’s morning routine.

Standing just far enough away so as not to bother her, Subaru, dressed in his butler uniform, scratched his head and let out a sigh as he stifled a rising yawn.

A night had passed since his meeting with Beatrice in the Forbidden Library, and it was now the morning of the third day. Having powered through yesterday by sleeping like a log all day, Subaru’s physical condition was still in absolute peak form.

He’d had a mountain of things he wanted to ask Beatrice from late night until early morning, but—

“It’s bad for my skin, so it’s time for me to sleep soon, in fact. In the first place, staying up this late resulted from being kept in your company, in fact.”

—And so, he was kicked out of the library by the visibly annoyed little girl.

Come to think of it, she was always in that room, but where in the world did she sleep in there? Aside from the bookshelves, there was Beatrice’s usual stepladder and a single desk that Subaru occasionally perched on. There was nothing else of note in that place.

Given her personality, there was no way she’d sleep directly on the floor, surely.

“I wonder if she has a bedroom. I’ve never seen her come out of one though! Not that I’m expecting some lucky pervert situation with a little girl like her.”

If it was being kept a secret, that was no fun.

He figured that next time he got the chance, he’d secretly follow Beatrice around for a day.

Assuming he broke out of the loop and managed to live peacefully in the mansion, of course.

—Finding yet another reason to stay positive and do his best, Subaru’s lips broke into a smile.

And then,

“You’re making a much purr-tier face now, aren’t you.”

Hearing the voice, he looked up to find a grey furball right in front of his eyes.

Rather, a small cat with a pink nose was floating there. It was Puck.

Making a gesture like a normal cat washing its face with its short paws, he said,

“Honestly, I couldn’t bear to look at you yesterday. So I’m a little relieved.”

“Right, sorry for worrying you. But my naive heart still hasn’t recovered at all. I need you to comfort it. Specifically,

 

fluff fluff fluff fluff.”

“Well, if you can put up that much of a front, I suppose you’re fine. I’m glad. It means it was worth Lia lending you her lap.”

Pulling the palm-sized cat closer, he indulged in his fluffball goodness to his heart’s content. Last time he’d realized the menace of his ears, but this time his focus was the tail. He specifically noticed the high fluff-rank of the tip and the base.

Gaining a supreme sensation in his fingertips, Subaru’s face melted into a dopey grin from the fluffiness as he met those black eyes.

“By any chance, did you see that lap pillow too?”

“Considering how long it was going on, yeah. Sitting on her knees for hours must have been tough, so I offered to swap out with her a few times, but… don’t worry. Lia never gave up her post till the very end.”

With Puck giving his seal of approval, Subaru couldn’t help but flush red with embarrassment. Seeing Subaru’s reaction, Puck went,

“Take that.”

“Ouch—?! Why’d you scratch me just now?!”

“The mother in me thought it was heartwarming, but the father in me felt an indescribable sense of displeasure toward you.”

“Torn between a woman’s heart and a man’s heart, huh? You’re pretty complicated yourself!”

“It’s tough being a parent to a cute daughter, you know. Ah, so put a little more distance between yourself and Lia, shoo, shoo.”

“You’ve resorted to blatant sabotage! This distance is my unyielding baseline! The feeling of being just out of reach even when I extend my hand is what makes it so refined, please understand.”

Groveling to somehow earn his forgiveness, Subaru successfully maintained the status quo.

Then, he looked over at Emilia once again. She seemed completely absorbed in her chat with the spirits, entirely oblivious to the back-and-forth between one guy and one animal that was shattering the morning peace.

Watching her serene profile that occasionally broke into a startlingly beautiful smile, Subaru suddenly muttered under his breath.

“—A silver-haired half-elf, huh.”

It was one of the traits of the Witch of Envy that Beatrice had told him about.

The origins of the witch who shook the world and was feared by absolutely everyone. Subaru, who was unfamiliar with such things, couldn’t even begin to guess how much of a burden it was to live while sharing traits with her. However, he could easily surmise that it was by no means an easy path.

And yet, she had still grown up with such an honest and straightforward personality. The reason she was able to live like a delicate flower whose loveliness remained unspoiled was probably because...

“She was incredibly blessed with the people around her. Or maybe…”

“It’s because her foster parent was so wonderful. Heh heh.”

Puffing out his chest with his paws on his hips, Puck chuckled while stroking his whiskers.

He was a cat who could read emotions. Combined with his soliloquy just now, he had likely grasped exactly what Subaru was thinking when he mumbled.

Beaten to the punch, Subaru closed his mouth, while Puck began to spin vertically round and round in midair,

“Well, it’s mostly due to the nature she was born with, though. I have no intention of telling you the whole story, but that girl has struggled ten thousand times more than you think. —But the fact that she’s still like that is exactly why she’s so precious.”

An objection didn’t even cross his mind.

It was a fact that Subaru didn’t know Emilia, and Puck had shared those unknown days with her. Furthermore, Subaru’s imagination was ultimately limited to that of a person who had been soaking in lukewarm water his whole life, whereas reality would easily trample over such imagination and strike.

When tossed about by fate, a person became just that powerless. It was something he had been made painfully aware of countless times since coming to this world, and Emilia had likely experienced it time and time again as well.

“Say, Puck, do you know about the Witch of Envy?”

“There’s not much that I don’t know.”

“Then there’s something I want to ask… what kind of situation would make someone use the Witch of Envy’s name? No, ‘use’ makes it sound bad. I guess I should say, when would someone borrow the Witch of Envy’s name?”

What revived in the back of his mind were the events of the loop on the very first day he was summoned.

He looked back on the very first time, the absolute beginning. Back then, Emilia had lied to the ignorant Subaru, claiming her name was “Satella.”

He had a vague idea of what her true intentions had been, but Subaru wanted someone else to validate it. And it would be even better if that someone was none other than her greatest confidant.

Not understanding the intent behind Subaru’s question, Puck fell silent for a moment before slowly opening his mouth,

“Either way, you do know it’s a death wish, right? People harboring grudges and bitterness toward the Witch are still endless, and the terror and despair etched into their hearts will never disappear either. Pretending to be the witch in the midst of all that… I guess you’d be nothing short of ny-uts.”

“I’ll take that.”

“?”

With a finger pointed at him, Puck floated a question mark.

Leaving him behind, Subaru pumped his fist internally at having gotten an opinion from Puck that validated his own deduction.

Exactly

.

 Giving the Witch’s name at that point would naturally get you treated like a total nutjob. It only hadn’t played out that way because Subaru was so absurdly ignorant of common sense, but normally, that’s exactly what would happen.

In that case, why had Emilia called herself that knowing it would happen?

“‘If I creep him out and make him think I’m crazy, I won’t have to drag him into something as dangerous as searching for my insignia’… it was that, right?”

To keep him away. He figured that was what she had been thinking.

The feelings of the Emilia who had already made that arrangement had vanished beyond the dimensions, and Subaru was the only one who knew about that exchange. And even this Subaru would never again have the chance to go and ask her true intentions.

But he had no choice but to believe that. Once he let himself think that, Subaru had already received enough from her to be fully convinced that it was the conclusion.

In short,

“Emilia-tan is seriously a Bodhisattva.”

“Don’t lump people in with things they don’t really understand.”

While Subaru was affirming Emilia’s boundless maternal love across dimensions, the girl herself approached with a wry smile.

Perhaps having finished her pleasant chat with the spirits, the pale lights that had been floating around her were nowhere to be seen. Instead, Puck, who had been swimming by Subaru’s side until just now, settled onto her shoulder.

“My usual spot, my usual spot. This really is the most relaxing place.”

“Yes, yes, welcome back. Sorry about this all the time. But when you’re around, Puck, the other little spirits get intimidated.”

“Intimidating spirits goes way past awe-inspiring and straight into ridiculous. It’s gonna cause misunderstandings like Puck being actually important!”

“Heh heh, I am important, even if I don’t look it. I demand to be revered more! Specifically, how about some dried sardines as an offering, nya.”

“You’re just making a beeline for cat food…”

Puck began swinging his head in a peek-a-boo boxing style. Stroking that grey head with her finger, Emilia turned to face Subaru once again.

Aware of the sheer beauty standing right in front of him, Subaru found himself almost involuntarily averting his eyes from her.

He felt awkward. Naturally.

After all, they had parted ways after she’d given him a lap pillow, he’d bawled his eyes out, and she’d stroked his head for hours. It had only been a single night since then.

What kind of face was the right one to show her? Honestly, he was in the mood to hug his pillow and roll around on his bed agonizing over it.

The fact that he’d come to see her anyway meant Subaru’s condition was serious. A severe state of Emilia-withdrawal. He could no longer survive without her.

“Umm, this is kind of embarrassing… How’s your health, are you okay?”

“I was having withdrawal symptoms, but you just cured them, so I’m perfect. What about you, Emilia-tan… uh, you know. Sorry for… all sorts of…”

Stumbling as he tried to voice his apology, Subaru swallowed his words and corrected himself.

“Thanks for everything. My head and heart were a murky labyrinth, but I kinda think they might have gotten a little better.”

“You don’t seem completely over it, but just wanting to get over it is a step forward. Yeah, as long as I could help even a little, that’s fine. If you feel like you’re wearing thin again, just tell me. Big sis will treat you right.”

Placing a hand on her chest, Emilia smiled as if to tease him.

That too was likely her considerate way of lightening Subaru’s guilt. Seeing her look so happy to act older, it almost felt like she was speaking from the heart, making his assumption waver a bit.

In any case,

“As long as you’re feeling energetic, that’s the best. You have to do your best at work today, after all. You went to sleep at a weird time, so are you feeling sleepy?”

“Rest assured. Shut-ins like me generally adopt a lifestyle of sleeping during the day and staying up at night. I’ve been a bit too healthy lately.”

“You say it sometimes, but what exactly is a ‘

shut-in’

1

?”

“It’s a badass who lights charcoal briquettes in his room and gambles on whether a pink-haired magician will fly in to save him.”

Honestly, that was the act of guys on a whole other stage of the soul.

Emilia nodded, slightly put off by the sheer bizarre nature of Subaru’s explanation. Watching her reaction, something suddenly occurred to him.

“Speaking of magicians, you’re one too, Emilia-tan. What kind of magic can you use?”

Asking “what kind of magic can you use?” was a conversation you could only have in another world. Subaru almost chuckled at the unexpectedly fantastical thing he’d just blurted out. However, Emilia shook her head at the question.

“Strictly speaking, I’m not a magician. In my case, like my contract with Puck, I’m a spirit user. I don’t use magic, I use spiritual arts. The principles are mostly the same, though.”

“So magicians and spirit users are different?”

Tilting his head, he looked at Puck sitting on her shoulder. Realizing the focus of the conversation had turned to him, the small cat started fiddling with the fur around his belly.

“Magicians use the mana inside their own bodies to cast magic. Conversely, spirit users use the mana in the atmosphere to cast their arts. Even if the resulting effects are similar, the path to get there is quite different.”

“And what kind of difference does that make, Professor?”

He raised a hand, throwing the question to his instructor, Puck.

The cat corrected his posture, his cheeks relaxing as if pleased.

“It boils down to whether or not you use a gate, so the difference is actually huge. In a magician’s case, the size and number of their gates directly correlate to their aptitude as a magician. But in a spirit user’s case, that doesn’t really matter. They use external mana, completely independent of their gates.”

“You take in mana from the outside through your gate, and use the mana stored inside to cast magic. And, spirit users don’t need to do that...”

Mentally digesting Puck’s explanation, Subaru paused mid-thought, tilting his head at a sudden “Huh?” moment.

“Wait, wait, wouldn’t that make things overwhelmingly advantageous for a spirit user? So a magician stores their fuel internally, but a spirit user has an all-you-can-use buffet of external fuel… Infinite MP wouldn’t even be a fair fight.”

“You catch on quick. But it’s not quite that convenient. The mana filling the atmosphere isn’t infinite, and…”

Puck broke off and raised his gaze to Emilia. Catching his look, she picked up where he left off.

“The strength of the arts a spirit user can handle depends entirely on the power of the contracted spirit they employ. Besides, contracting with a spirit is a pretty rare thing to begin with, so I don’t think you can really say one is better compared to the other.”

“Hmm… But if you’re contracted with a powerful spirit, you’re pretty well set, right? Emilia-tan, Puck’s actually a real big shot, ain’t he?”

“Well, I wouldn’t deny that it’s faster to count from the top, nyau.”

“You seem all laid-back, but you don’t hold back when you say things… You never waver when it comes to asserting yourself.”

Subaru fancied himself an expert on having a strong ego, but even he was amazed by Puck’s unshakable nature. It must have been a difference in experience. Between a greenhorn and a Great Spirit, the years they’d cultivated it were worlds apart.

For all that, the Great Spirit was bashfully laughing in a very pleased manner, as if he wasn’t used to being praised. Subaru pointed at him.

“Come to think of it, what kind of spirit are you, Puck? You were tossing out ice left and right at the loot house… but if memory serves, I thought ice wasn’t an element to begin with.”

When he had received a lecture from Roswaal in the bath a while back, the orthodox four types Subaru had heard about were Fire, Water, Earth, and Wind. Added to that were only the cursed Yin and Yang branches.

The one who answered Subaru’s question was Emilia, who had been stroking the embarrassed Puck’s head. She turned her right palm upwards, and—

“It’s ice, but this is actually Fire mana. Fire is a mana that primarily relates to heat, so broadly speaking, both hot and cold fall under the Fire category.”

With a sound like the atmosphere cracking, an icicle appeared slightly above her palm.

The icicle, roughly the size of a traffic cone, pointed its sharp tip toward him and began to spin like a drill.

“You probably didn’t mean anything by it, but that’s scary?! If I had a phobia of sharp objects, I’d be wetting my pants right now!”

“Ah, sorry. I just tried to give an easy-to-understand explanation and it slipped out… It’s fine that I summoned it, but now I don’t know what to do with it.”

“And your idea of aimlessly threatening me with it is dangerous! I prefer my Emilia-tan to be modest and sweet, thanks!”

“Yes, yes.”

Brushing him off with a nod, Emilia clapped her hands, and the icicle dissipated into mist.

It didn’t melt or shatter; it literally turned to powder and evaporated.

It was a strange mechanic, but its fantasy elements ceaselessly tugged at Subaru’s curiosity.

His itching anticipation must have shown on his face. Puck, who had been watching the silent Subaru, suddenly asked,

“Hmm, do you want to use magic by any chance?”

“Can I?! Oh man! In that case! Ultimate Annihilation Spell…”

“No, you can’t. Whether it’s magic or spiritual arts, you can’t underestimate the basics. Magic wasn’t built in a day.”

Smacking down Subaru’s flared-up curiosity from directly above, Puck crossed his arms. His momentum broken, Subaru slumped his shoulders. Perhaps taking pity on him, Puck tweaked his whiskers and added, “But…”

“I might be able to let you have a simple trial experience, maybe?”

“Meaning?”

“Basically, you want to use magic, so either Lia or I just have to assist you. We’ll utilize the mana inside your body, and cast the magic through you, Subaru. From our perspective, it’s just a matter of whether the mana comes from the atmosphere or from you, and the magic itself will come out of your gate. How about it?”

“Hold on, Puck, don’t just casually promise things like that. It might be dangerous, you know.”

Emilia, his partner, rebuked Puck’s sweet temptation. She seemed to genuinely be worried about the safety of the act, but—

“Sorry, Emilia-tan. I’m glad you’re worried about me. Super glad, but… I’m doing it!”

Giving a thumbs-up with a flash of his teeth, Subaru shot Emilia a triumphant smile.

At Subaru’s attitude, which completely eliminated all negative elements like anxiety or concern, Emilia couldn’t hide her surprise and blinked several times.

“W-Why go that far…?”

“Even if I know it’s dangerous, even if the risks are obvious, there are times when a man just has to do it… If I miss a chance like this where I might be able to use magic, there’s no point in me being summoned to another world!”

A roar of the soul with a clenched fist.

Right now, Subaru was more pumped up than he had ever been since coming to this other world. Thus far, the only otherworldly blessing he’d enjoyed was the eye candy of being surrounded by gorgeous people. For Subaru, if he missed out on this, he wouldn’t even be able to talk about the ‘other world’ experience.

Realizing it was useless to oppose Subaru’s enthusiasm, Emilia gave in, emphasizing, “If I think it’s dangerous, I’m stopping you immediately.”

Receiving that warning with a great big smile, Subaru turned back to Puck.

“What should I do first? Do I need to draw a magic circle, or offer Beako as a sacrifice?”

“I’m just glad you seem to be getting along with Betty. Right, let’s start by checking your affinity, Subaru. We can’t start unless we know what kind of magic you can use.”

Hearing Puck’s suggestion, Subaru’s previously bright expression clouded over in an instant. Puck blinked his black eyes at the prominent reaction, but Subaru just waved his hand and ambiguously mumbled, “No,”

"M-y a-f-f-i-n-i-t-y i-s p-r-o-b-a-b-l-y F-i-r-e, r-i-g-h-t?"

“Why are you suddenly speaking in broken sentences?”

At Emilia’s question, Subaru slowly shook his head side to side, so stiffly it almost made a dull creaking sound. He didn’t want to remember any more than that.

But paying no mind to Subaru’s feelings, Puck took off from Emilia’s shoulder and hovered right in front of Subaru’s face.

“Excuse me, then.”

“Whoa, what is this new sensation?”

Stretching out his tail that rivaled the length of his own small body, Puck pressed its tip against Subaru’s forehead. He was likely inspecting the mana inside Subaru’s body.

He recalled that when Puck communicated telepathically with Emilia before, they pressed their foreheads together. Rather than the difference in treatment, he just felt jealous of Puck’s luck in getting to press his forehead against Emilia’s.

“Even trying to brush it off like that won’t change reality… No, wait, wait, let’s think positively like I always do. Thinking back, wasn’t Roswaal’s attitude pretty unnatural back then? Yeah, he was jealous of the rare magical talent sleeping inside of me. Oh, shit! Yeah, that guy was jealous of me. That’s why he fed me a bunch of lies to try and close off my brilliant path as a magician…”

“How rare. You’re dead set in the Yin affinity.”

“I want a second opinion—!!”

Subaru fell into despair at having it certified by a different person across dimensions.

Unless Puck and Roswaal had colluded on this matter, he had no choice but to believe the result. What were the chances that this carefree cat—who seemed to embody the phrase ‘Others are others, our house is our house!’ that Subaru’s real mother used to say so often—would be jealous of Subaru’s talent and lie about it?

“So I’m specialized in debuffs… I really wanted to shoot off lighting like crazy and blow away an army of ten thousand, though…”

“Ah, you also have absolutely zero talent. Your gate is small, and the number of them is at least slightly decent, I guess? A lot of them aren’t fully open, so the ventilation seems pretty bad, too.”

“I know, shut up! Don’t talk about me like I’m some room with unwashed screen doors! By the way, if we were to put a number on my talent, what would it be?”

“If you devoted yourself exclusively to magical training for twenty years, you might just about reach the cusp of being first-rate, I suppose.”

“Betting half my life just to be sub-par… I give up on this path…!”

Emilia looked exasperated at Subaru’s tearful declaration of giving up on his dream. But it couldn’t be helped. To Subaru, words like ‘effort’ and ‘hard work’ were things he didn’t want to look at, so much so that they’d have claw marks over them in his dictionary.

However, setting those feelings aside,

“I still want to do the hands-on magic trial, so please. What do I do?”

“Since it’s the Yin affinity… that was a bit unexpected. Let’s see, what was a simple Yin magic spell again, Lia?”

“With Yin affinity, I think the blinding spell ‘Shamak’ falls under that, but… sorry, I’m not too confident.”

Emilia lamented her lack of capability. In front of her, Puck clapped his paws together, “Ah, that’s right.”

“Shamak, huh. Bringing up something rarely used, are we. Well then, let’s make casting that our goal for now.”

“Wait, wait, wait. Don’t just proceed like it’s a given, that’s a problem. First off, what kind of spell is this Shamak? If I use it without knowing the effect and some incomprehensible power turns me into a frog, what then? If that happens, you’ll have to turn me into a prince with a kiss, Emilia-tan.”

“Is it just me who feels like the beginning and end of that did not connect?”

Stared at with half-lidded eyes, Subaru shrank back in humility. Meanwhile, Puck nodded, acknowledging that Subaru had a point.

“That’s true. It might be a little scary to try using a magic you know nothing about. Okay, I’ll show you. This is Shamak.”

Waving his short arms, Puck swiftly completed the incantation.

And then, suddenly, Subaru’s vision was swallowed by darkness. Right after blinking, even though he opened his eyes, his vision remained as dark as if his eyelids were still shut.

Without thinking, he let out a small voice of surprise, but even the voice he’d supposedly raised didn’t reach his ears. The darkness that had been generated completely severed Subaru’s vision and his connection to the outside world, sending a sensation akin to terror running down his spine.

“Alright, all done.”

“Mommmyyy… wait, huh? It’s back?”

“It’s back. More importantly, Subaru… didn’t you just cry out for your mommy because you were so anxious?”

“I didn’t do anything so unmanly?! That just now, y’know, it was that thing! That thing where you accidentally call your teacher ‘Mom’ at school!”

His sight had returned, and seeing the absolute beauty and the small cat lined up in front of him made him sigh in relief.

Touching his own eyelids, he confirmed there were no changes there, then said,

“So that blinding trick just now is the magic called Shamak. It’s subtle, but couldn’t you expect some pretty serious results from it?”

“Not really. Unless it’s an opponent weaker than or equal to you, it’ll just get repelled by the sheer difference in strength, and it won’t last long either. If I’m casting it on you, Subaru, I could force you to spend your entire life in darkness, though.”

“Your train of thought is scary?! You wouldn’t even need to do it that long, I’m totally confident I’d become a groggy wreck if that state lasted just a single day.”

Offering a wry smile, Subaru secretly hid his trembling fists behind his back.

Still fresh in his memory was how, the moment he experienced the sensation of everything fading away, he was struck by a sense of desolation, as if he had been completely left behind by the world.

Like he was entirely alone in the entire world, thoroughly convinced he didn’t have a single ally—suddenly recalling that time, his hands trembled.

How pathetic, he clicked his tongue, and pulling up a smile, Subaru said,

“Anyway, whether it’s effective or not aside, it means I can use that magic right now, right? I’d like to try it right away, please!”

“Sure thing. Alright, I’ll assist. In the unlikely event that his mana goes berserk and Subaru bursts, your clothes will get dirty, Lia, so stand back.”

“That really is just an ‘unlikely’ event, right?! That’s like an almost impossible failure case, isn’t it?!”

Puck smiled amiably in silence, and Emilia, looking a little grim, left him with a “Don’t push yourself too hard” before actually putting some distance between them.

In this highly anxiety-inducing setting, things began to progress, completely leaving behind the aura of Subaru who had started to backpedal.

Puck sat on the crown of Subaru’s short black hair, adjusting the position of his rump,

“Your head is all prickly, it’s not very comfortable to sit on.”

“I just never thought the day would come when I’d have someone ride on it. I can’t offer you a cushion for hospitality, but make yourself at home.”

“Nah, I already miss the inside of Lia’s hair, so I’ll finish this up quick and head back. So then, are you mentally prepared?”

At the question, Subaru hesitated for only a fraction of a second. But he quickly twisted his cheeks into the shape of a smile and slowly nodded.

There were plenty of anxiety factors, but even so, he couldn’t go against his curiosity.

Receiving Subaru’s affirmative response, Puck gave a single large nod as well.

Then, suddenly, Subaru was struck by a sensation like his entire body was growing hot. A feeling circulating through his body that was different from blood—this invisible, raging torrent ravaging his insides was likely what they called mana.

Guided by something transmitting from Puck on top of his head, he could feel the energy inside his body moving with direction.

“Subaru, try to imagine it. Right now, I’m grabbing the flow of mana inside your body and moving it. You need to spit a portion of it out of your body through your gate. It will take shape outside—becoming a black cloud like before.”

“Imagine, imagine, huh. Leave it to me, I’m great at fantasizing.”

Slightly misinterpreting Puck’s advice, Subaru sought a destination for the energy writhing inside of him within his delusions.

A gate—imagining what was called a door in the center of his body. The gate pushed open its heavy doors, causing the energy from the inside to overflow to the outside. That energy spilled out, and conforming to Subaru’s will, sublimated into a phenomenon—

“Oh, this is troubling. The gate suddenly—”

Just as they reached the final stage, Puck suddenly murmured that.

He wasn’t given the time to utter the question “What did you—”

Immediately after—

“Both of you?!”

Emilia screamed, and a few seconds later, a corner of the garden at Roswaal Manor was completely engulfed in an explosively erupting black mist.

—Though he didn’t end up bursting, it was, ultimately, a massive failure.
